beats.say: Every account needs its own long password. Nobody can remember them all.
Never reuse a password: when one site leaks, attackers try it on all your accounts.
The organisation's password manager creates a strong password per account and stores it in an encrypted vault.
You remember just one long master password and protect the vault with two-step verification.

scenes.prompt: Is this a safe place for a password?

cards.explain: The file is not encrypted: anyone who gets into the computer sees every password at once.
The password sits in the encrypted vault and opens only with your master password.
A messenger is not a vault. If the phone is lost or the account taken over, the passwords go too.

body.text: 3 members. Website admin panel, social media account.

cards.explain: The team shares passwords in an encrypted vault, and access can be removed at any time.

scenes.title: Password requests
scenes.intro: Today several people ask you for passwords. Answer each one on your phone.

body.text: Hi! Could you type the website admin panel password here? I'm posting today's news.

steps.say: She is your colleague and really needs access.

actions.label: Type the password
actions.feedback: The password stays in the chat and can leak if a phone is lost. Share it from the vault.

actions.label: I'll share it with you in the vault
actions.feedback: Right. In the vault the password stays encrypted, and access can be removed when needed.

actions.label: I'll send it by SMS
actions.feedback: SMS is not encrypted either and stays on the phone. Share passwords only through the vault.

subject.text: Elnur Kərimov shared a vault with you

body.text: Sign in to view the "Finance" vault:

steps.say: You were not expecting a share.

actions.label: Open link
actions.feedback: A real share shows up inside the ParolSeyf app itself. This link is hunting for your master password.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Right: the address is not ParolSeyf's. Open the app yourself to check for shares.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: You are safe, but colleagues may get the same mail. Report it.

body.text: We found an error in your vault. To restore it, type your master password and the code you receive here.

actions.label: Type the master password
actions.feedback: The master password unlocks every password you have. No support team ever asks for it.

actions.label: Block
actions.feedback: Right. Nobody, not even technical support, asks for your master password or code.

actions.label: Report
actions.feedback: Great. Tell security as well so they can warn colleagues.

title.text: This password is used on 3 accounts

body.text: The same password is saved for İşPoçt, the office portal and the Kontakto page.

actions.label: Change passwords
actions.feedback: Right. The generator makes a separate password for each account, so one leak opens nothing else.

actions.label: Later
actions.feedback: A reused password is a weakness attackers love. One leak would open all three accounts.

scenes.prompt: Create a master password: a long phrase of at least 15 characters.
tips: Join four or five random words with spaces
Avoid names, birthdays and famous quotes

pairs.right: The one password that opens the vault
Lets a team share passwords safely

scenes.explain: The manager remembers the passwords; you only guard the master password.

question.prompt: Three people in your department run the same social media account. How should they share the password?

options.label: Separate logins if possible, otherwise a shared vault
options.feedback: Right. When someone leaves the team, their access is removed in one step.

options.label: Post the password in the team chat
options.feedback: A password posted in a group chat stays there for years, and new members see it too.

options.label: Write it on a sticky note on the monitor
options.feedback: Anyone who walks in can see the password and take a photo.

scenes.explain: Even for a shared account, the password lives in the vault, not in chats or on paper.

points: A separate password for every account: the manager creates and remembers it.
Share passwords in a shared vault, never in a chat.
Never tell anyone your master password, and protect the vault with two-step verification.
